message.content:
The given statements define a directed graph of ancestor-to-descendant relations (an edge \(A \to B\) means "\(A\) is an ancestor of \(B\)"). Transitive paths in this graph preserve the ancestor relationship.

Joe has exactly one direct outgoing edge: Joe \(\to\) Roger. All subsequent reachable nodes (Roger through Teresa, Maria, Lawrence, and onward) are therefore descendants of Joe. In particular, there is a path Joe \(\to \dots \to\) Adam.

Roy has exactly one direct outgoing edge: Roy \(\to\) Justin. All subsequent reachable nodes (Justin through Sophia, Kimberly, …, Mary, and onward) are therefore descendants of Roy. In particular, there is a path Roy \(\to \dots \to\) Adam.

Consequently, Adam is a descendant of both Joe and Roy: Joe and Roy share a common descendant.

No statement supplies an incoming edge to Joe or to Roy. Therefore neither person has any ancestor in the graph, so Joe and Roy share no common ancestor. There is likewise no directed path from Joe to Roy or from Roy to Joe, eliminating the possibilities that one is an ancestor or descendant of the other.

The only relation that holds is that they share a common descendant.
